bug_semantics: The product edit and save paths trusted a user-controlled numeric product ID without binding the lookup to Auth::user()->company_id. GET /product/update/{id} loaded Product::find($id) and rendered the record's commercial fields, while POST /product/save loaded Product::find($data['id']) and then overwrote that record's company_id with the attacker's company, allowing an authenticated tenant to disclose and take over another tenant's product. ProductUpdateController and ProductCreateController also did not inherit MainController, so they did not receive its auth and locked middleware.
flaw_origin: Commit 0a2eeb13e0a020bc59c7622527c49a15087869da first wrote both identifier-trusting operations in app/Http/Controllers/ProductController.php: Product::find($id) in edit() and Product::find($request->id) in save(), and made POST /product/save reachable. Its direct parent has neither method nor either lookup. Later tenancy work made those unscoped lookups cross-company: 8c661622c387b0c0a7f76ad56f545d780ebf6a91 added product.company_id without scoping the reads, and e0e204da8ca57b0865b7e5df8cd495b2bc76d6e2 assigned Auth::user()->company_id after the unscoped save lookup. c028795fe359e5eb750956325dbddae4ff567093, the 5f6379ac899e4705aba272da62582ade30a5a655 plus 9e07ae4c618e326a5af39b742e2bc0984906c28d sequence, and 65f6b9f961efe533b4d3f20f1eddad132fe8ef1d subsequently relocated or reconstituted the same flawed operations and therefore are not BICs.
ai_marker: absent — the exact 0a2eeb13e0a020bc59c7622527c49a15087869da commit object names author and committer Gustavo Novaro <gnovaro@gmail.com>, and its complete message is 'Product basic CRUD' with no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI-attribution trailer.
evidence: Official CVE record https://cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/CVE-2026-19734 identifies Roskus Prospero Flow CRM versions >=0 and <5.4.7 as affected and names app/Http/Controllers/Product/ProductUpdateController.php, app/Http/Controllers/Product/ProductCreateController.php, and app/Repositories/ProductRepository.php. The Secur0 CNA technical advisory https://secur0.com/en/cna/cve-list/cve-2026-19734-idor-in-prospero-flow-crm-allows-cross-tenant-product-disclosure-and-hijacking describes the GET /product/update/{id} disclosure and POST /product/save takeover and identifies f36c2a115f4c28c82181f1798c01582ae953b932 as the 5.4.7 patch.

git log -S'Product::find($id)' and git log -S'Product::find($request->id)' trace both vulnerable lookups to 0a2eeb13e0a020bc59c7622527c49a15087869da, whose focused diff adds edit() with Product::find($id), save() with Product::find($request->id), and the POST /product/save route in app/Http/Controllers/ProductController.php and routes/web.php. Direct-parent tree 91c994d586980f6d7a98d0227ef2a5e39523b946 contains only ProductController::index(), no edit() or save(), and no POST /product/save route, proving both vulnerable lines and their save attack path absent in the immediate parent.

The tenant-impact lifecycle is source-verified rather than inferred from later blame. Commit 8c661622c387b0c0a7f76ad56f545d780ebf6a91 introduces database/migrations/2021_06_24_114555_create_product_table.php with nullable product.company_id while leaving the already-unscoped ProductController lookups intact. Commit e0e204da8ca57b0865b7e5df8cd495b2bc76d6e2 makes product.company_id non-null and replaces the save TODO with $product->company_id = Auth::user()->company_id immediately after Product::find($request->id), enabling a caller-selected record to be transferred to the caller's tenant.

Move/refactor decomposition rules out the advisory's later sink locations as BICs. c028795fe359e5eb750956325dbddae4ff567093 removes the save body from ProductController and copies it into Product\ProductSaveController. Then 5f6379ac899e4705aba272da62582ade30a5a655 removes ProductController::edit(), creates an empty ProductUpdateController, and changes /product/edit/{id} to /product/update/{id}; two minutes later 9e07ae4c618e326a5af39b742e2bc0984906c28d restores the same Product::find($id) read in that new controller. Finally, 65f6b9f961efe533b4d3f20f1eddad132fe8ef1d removes the save sequence from ProductSaveController and recreates it in new app/Repositories/ProductRepository.php. None first wrote the flawed ID-trusting operations.

Immediately before the fix, blame/tree checks at parent c0ac18d4236dfa224a9abc8fc11b80b2066b5d35 show app/Http/Controllers/Product/ProductUpdateController.php:17 as Product::find($id) and app/Repositories/ProductRepository.php:18-20 as Product::find($data['id']) followed by company_id overwrite. ProductUpdateController does not extend MainController, whereas app/Http/Controllers/MainController.php middleware() returns auth and locked.

The first-party patch https://github.com/Roskus/prospero-flow-crm/commit/f36c2a115f4c28c82181f1798c01582ae953b932 changes ProductUpdateController to extend MainController and replaces its lookup at line 18 with Product::where('company_id', Auth::user()->company_id)->findOrFail($id). It likewise replaces ProductRepository.php:18 with the company-scoped findOrFail lookup and changes version.php from APP_VERSION 5.4.6 in direct parent c0ac18d4236dfa224a9abc8fc11b80b2066b5d35 to APP_VERSION 5.4.7. The same commit is both the advisory-named patch and the direct source fix.

Tag ancestry and tree checks establish the release boundary: v1.0.0, v2.0.1, and v4.6.0 contain 0a2eeb13e0a020bc59c7622527c49a15087869da and the later tenancy/refactor history but not f36c2a115f4c28c82181f1798c01582ae953b932. The v4.6.0 tree has both raw Product::find calls and APP_VERSION 4.6.0. The earliest tag containing the fix is v5.5.3 (https://github.com/Roskus/prospero-flow-crm/releases/tag/v5.5.3), whose tree has company-scoped lookups, MainController inheritance, and APP_VERSION 5.5.3; the untagged fix commit itself establishes the 5.4.7 patched boundary.

reasoning: The causal invariant is that a product lookup controlled by the request must be constrained to the authenticated tenant before any data is returned or overwritten. 0a2eeb13e0a020bc59c7622527c49a15087869da is the smallest BIC because it is the single commit that first wrote both unscoped Product::find operations and made the save route functional; its direct parent has neither operation. The later product.company_id schema and assignment commits supplied the tenant boundary and amplified the save operation into cross-company reassignment, but they inherited rather than authored the unscoped lookup flaw. The apparent 2021-2023 introducers are explicitly decomposed moves: c028795fe359e5eb750956325dbddae4ff567093 relocates save, 5f6379ac899e4705aba272da62582ade30a5a655 plus 9e07ae4c618e326a5af39b742e2bc0984906c28d relocates read, and 65f6b9f961efe533b4d3f20f1eddad132fe8ef1d relocates save again. f36c2a115f4c28c82181f1798c01582ae953b932 closes both data paths by applying tenant-scoped findOrFail queries, adds MainController inheritance for middleware enforcement, and advances 5.4.6 to 5.4.7; affected and fixed tag trees agree with that boundary. The exact 0a2eeb13e0a020bc59c7622527c49a15087869da commit object contains only a human author/committer and no AI marker, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
